core_obligations: Construct the map A^p(X -> Spec(k)) -> CH_{-p}(X) by c -> c cap [Spec(k)] (proof lines 14193-14194).

Construct the converse: given alpha in CH_{-p}(X), write alpha = sum n_i [X_i], form the proper g : Disjoint X_i -> X and the flat f : Disjoint X_i -> Spec(k) of relative dimension -p, let nu multiply the i-th component by n_i, and define c_alpha using the bivariant classes f^* and the proper pushforward g_* (proof lines 14197-14224).

Show the two constructions are mutually inverse: one direction is c_alpha cap [Spec(k)] = alpha, and for the other it suffices by the bivariant-class axiom to compare c cap [X'] with c_alpha cap [X'] for integral X' locally of finite type over k, where p' : X' -> Spec(k) is flat of relative dimension dim X' and hence [X'] = (p')^*[Spec(k)], so equality on [Spec(k)] propagates (proof lines 14227-14240).
proof_roadmap: One direction from capping with the point class (proof lines 14193-14194).
Build the bivariant class attached to a cycle class out of flat pullback, a multiplication by multiplicities and proper pushforward (proof lines 14197-14224).
Check the two constructions are inverse by testing on integral X' (proof lines 14227-14240).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts a canonical identification A^p(X -> Spec(k)) = CH_{-p}(X) for a scheme X locally of finite type over a field k and every p (statement lines 14182-14190). One direction is immediate from capping with the class of the point, but the converse must build a bivariant class out of an arbitrary cycle class alpha: writing alpha = sum n_i [X_i], the author forms the proper map g from the disjoint union of the X_i to X and the flat map f from that disjoint union to Spec(k) of relative dimension -p, multiplies by the integer n_i through a bivariant class nu on the disjoint union, and obtains the required class as g_* o nu o f^*, using that flat pullback and proper pushforward are bivariant operations (proof lines 14193-14224). The mutual inverses are then checked by reducing, through the bivariant-class axiom for the empty class, to integral X' for which the structure morphism is flat of relative dimension dim(X'), so that [X'] = (p')^*[Spec(k)] (proof lines 14227-14240). The construction of the converse class rather than the identification itself is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
